clue.text: High-flyer in bleakest relationship

indicators.note: in signals that the answer sits inside the run of letters of the following words

explanation.surface: Someone ambitious is caught in a very gloomy relationship.
explanation.definitionFit: A kestrel is a small falcon that hovers high over fields, so a bird is literally a high-flyer.

clue.text: I'd cook special stew, constantly changing in form

indicators.note: to stew things is to cook them in a jumbled mixture, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A recipe: cook up a special stew whose form keeps changing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stew' reads as a noun, the dish; it is a verb telling you to jumble I'D COOK SPECIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A kaleidoscope shows shifting patterns, so the adjective describes something whose shape keeps varying.

clue.text: Suppression of information from south European battlefield

parts.note: Crecy, in northern France, was the site of the 1346 English victory

explanation.surface: News from a southern European battlefield is censored.
explanation.walkthrough: Crécy is where Edward III's longbowmen won in 1346.
explanation.definitionFit: Secrecy is the keeping of things hidden, the withholding of information.

clue.text: Give the lie to extremely reasonable objection

indicators.note: extremely means the extremes, the first and last letters of reasonable

parts.note: but is an objection, as in no ifs or buts

explanation.surface: A very reasonable objection exposes a falsehood.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebut is to refute, to give the lie to a claim.

clue.text: Bound over, this being one's game?

definitions.text: Bound over, this being one's game?

parts.words: Bound over, this being one's game?
parts.note: read not as a court bind-over but literally: a playground game where each player bounds over the others' backs

explanation.surface: A defendant bound over by the court treats it as a game.
explanation.definitionFit: In this children's game players vault over each other's stooping backs, so jumping over is the whole game.

clue.text: Man on board given work by mistake

parts.note: bish is British slang for a blunder
op is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: An employee aboard ship is given a job by mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: BISH is informal British for a mistake or botch. 'Board' is a chessboard, not a ship or a committee.
explanation.definitionFit: The bishop is one of the chess pieces, a figure that stands on the chessboard.

clue.text: Given hearing, accept old PM's regulation

indicators.note: given hearing means the word for accept is heard rather than seen

parts.note: to buy an idea is to accept it
Andrew Bonar Law was British Prime Minister in 1922-23

explanation.surface: Agreeing to a former Prime Minister's rule once it has been heard.
explanation.walkthrough: Bonar Law was a British Prime Minister in the 1920s.
explanation.definitionFit: A bye-law is a local regulation made by a council or company.

clue.text: Agree to contribute regularly

definitions.meaning: to endorse or support a view
to pay a regular sum, as to a magazine or charity

explanation.surface: Someone signs up to pay a regular donation.
explanation.definitionFit: Subscribe means both to assent to an opinion and to pay money periodically for something.

clue.text: Assessment of confused type in plant

indicators.note: in says the confused type sits inside the plant

parts.note: an onion is a plant
pi is printers' term for jumbled type

explanation.surface: A judgement on a muddled sort of plant.
explanation.walkthrough: Pi (or pie) is printers' jargon for type spilled into a jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: An opinion is a view or judgement, an assessment of something.

clue.text: Instrument trainee artist's taken in to study at night

indicators.note: taken in says the trainee and artist are placed within the instrument

parts.note: a lute is a stringed musical instrument
a cub is a novice, as in a cub reporter
RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: A musical instrument is used by a trainee artist studying through the night.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucubrate is a formal verb for working or studying late, by lamplight.

clue.text: Barrister's description of Macbeth's candle

definitions.meaning: a barrister's case papers from the solicitor are called his or her ...
Macbeth says 'Out, out, ... candle!', calling life short-lived

explanation.surface: A lawyer quotes Shakespeare's line about the candle of life.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief is the document instructing a barrister, and also an adjective meaning short, the word Macbeth applies to his candle.

clue.text: Game played by chirpy type in Paris?

parts.note: in Paris things are French
a cricket is an insect known for its chirping

explanation.surface: A cheerful character in Paris plays a game.
explanation.walkthrough: French cricket is an informal garden version of cricket, the bat-and-ball game, where the batsman's legs are the wicket.
explanation.definitionFit: This informal children's version of cricket is a game.

clue.text: Popular record originally thought unsuitable

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: originally means the start, so only the first letter of thought is used

explanation.surface: A hit single is at first considered inappropriate.
explanation.definitionFit: Inept means clumsy or lacking skill, so it is a near synonym of unsuitable in the sense of not fit for the job.

clue.text: Anatole defends a man's rights of citizenship

indicators.note: defends pictures the writer standing guard around something, so it encloses it

parts.note: Anatole France was the French novelist
his means belonging to a man

explanation.surface: The French writer Anatole stands up for a person's civic rights.
explanation.walkthrough: Anatole France (1844-1924) was a Nobel-winning French novelist, so his surname is supplied.
explanation.definitionFit: The franchise is the right to vote, the core entitlement of being a citizen.

clue.text: For example, living death doctor observed during year in county

indicators.note: in says the doctor and year group sits within the county

parts.note: Oxon is the abbreviation for Oxfordshire, an English county

indicators.note: observed during says the doctor is seen inside the year abbreviation

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor, watching a deathly patient through a year in the shires, offers an example.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxon is the short form of Oxfordshire, a county west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A living death joins two contradictory terms, which is exactly the figure of speech named here, so the phrase is an instance of it.

clue.text: New bosses spouting tediously about current preoccupation

indicators.note: new means the letters of bosses are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current
going on about something means talking at tedious length

explanation.surface: Fresh bosses drone on about their current fixation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges BOSSES into OBSESS; 'going on about' gives ON.
explanation.definitionFit: An obsession is a fixation that fills the mind, a strong preoccupation.

clue.text: Choose fellow, sound for external courses?

indicators.note: sound says the words for choose and fellow are spoken, not spelt

parts.note: pick means choose, and Nick is a man's name standing for a fellow

explanation.surface: Picking a companion who seems right for an outdoor course.
explanation.definitionFit: A meal eaten outside is literally a set of courses served outdoors, a witty description of an outdoor meal.

clue.text: Lay on rest in broadcast for a vocalist

indicators.note: on in a down clue says the song sits on top of the other piece

parts.note: a lay is a song or ballad

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, so the letters of rest are scattered

parts.note: fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: A singer has a lie-down during a radio broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: A songster is a singer, especially a skilled one.

clue.text: Braque, for one, in fashion again

indicators.note: in says the word for again is placed inside the word for fashion

parts.note: to cut is to fashion or shape
bis is Latin for twice, used for an encore, so again

explanation.surface: The painter Braque is back in vogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In fashion' looks like one phrase meaning trendy; split it, with 'in' the container signal and 'fashion' the verb cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Georges Braque co-founded Cubism with Picasso, so he is an example of a painter of that school.

clue.text: Device to contact British general by?

parts.note: Robert E Lee was the Confederate general
per means by, as in per post

explanation.surface: A gadget for getting hold of a British general?
explanation.definitionFit: A bleeper is a pager, a device that beeps to summon someone.

clue.text: Daily flak mostly associated with millennium feature

parts.note: the Millennium Dome was London's landmark built for 2000

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter of the word for flak

parts.note: stick means criticism, as in giving someone stick

explanation.surface: Daily criticism goes with a feature built for the millennium.
explanation.walkthrough: The Millennium Dome is the large tent-like building in Greenwich, London. A daily is British for a cleaner who comes in each day.
explanation.definitionFit: A daily, a cleaner or home help, is also called a domestic, a household servant.

clue.text: Like Hans Andersen and his diversified characters

indicators.note: diversified means varied, so the characters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Andersen and his varied fictional characters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters' looks like story figures; it means the letters of AND HIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Hans Christian Andersen was from Denmark, so the adjective describing him is his nationality.

clue.text: Coercive group from media go to Scotland

parts.note: the press is the news media
gang is the Scots word for go

explanation.surface: A gang of journalists heads north of the border to put on pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: A press gang forced men into naval service, so it is a group that compels others.

clue.text: Capital a small number invested in Hawaii

indicators.note: invested in says the pieces are placed within the state abbreviation

parts.note: HI is the postal code of Hawaii
no is the abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: A modest sum of capital is put into a business in Hawaii.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanoi is the capital city of Vietnam.

clue.text: Bird's name attached to priestess of Aphrodite

parts.note: Hero was the priestess of Aphrodite loved by Leander

explanation.surface: A bird named after Aphrodite's priestess.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Hero, Aphrodite's priestess at Sestos, was visited nightly by Leander swimming the Hellespont.
explanation.definitionFit: A heron is a long-legged wading bird.

clue.text: Island beginning to celebrate All Fools' Day

indicators.note: beginning to means only the first letter of celebrate is used

parts.note: April Fools' Day is 1 April, written Apr I with a Roman one

explanation.surface: An island party to mark April Fools' Day.
explanation.walkthrough: All Fools' Day is 1 April; written as Apr plus the Roman numeral I.
explanation.definitionFit: Capri is an island in the Bay of Naples.

clue.text: Get engaged, wanting security after season out West

indicators.note: after puts the security word behind the shortened season
out means the letter for West is removed from the season

parts.note: winter is one of the four seasons
a lock keeps things secure

explanation.surface: A couple get engaged in the West, needing security after the winter.
explanation.definitionFit: To interlock is for parts to engage with each other, like meshing gears.

clue.text: Limb discovered in local office

definitions.meaning: a limb of a tree, a bough
a local outlet of a bank or firm

explanation.surface: A severed limb turns up in a branch office.
explanation.definitionFit: Branch means both a bough of a tree and a local office of a larger organisation.

clue.text: Curl right round fireplace

indicators.note: round says the abbreviation for right goes around the fireplace

parts.note: an ingle is a fireplace, as in inglenook

explanation.surface: A curl of hair lies right around the hearth.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringlet is a lock of hair hanging in a curl.
